verdict_reason: The finish rewrite and the pre-rename leftover move close the original split, but a lock waiter can still create a second .eck and a symlinked .c3 is still written through by consult.
reply_markdown:
## Q1. Two folders

Two `c3 finish` processes no longer recreate `.eck/`. `write_answer` goes through `write_in` (`crates/c3/src/finish/mod.rs:182`), which remaps a legacy path once `.eck` is gone (`crates/c3/src/state_dir.rs:390`, `crates/c3/src/state_dir.rs:1543`).

A waiter that gives up while the holder is still before the rename can. `MoveLock::acquire` waits 10s (`crates/c3/src/state_dir.rs:105`, `crates/c3/src/state_dir.rs:488`) and `after_failure` (`crates/c3/src/state_dir.rs:784`) keeps `.eck` when `.c3` is absent. The holder is still inside `migrate_legacy` (`crates/c3/src/state_dir.rs:713` through `crates/c3/src/state_dir.rs:735`). `c3 explain` with no `--out`, and `c3 index` when the Surreal feature is on, then `create_dir_all` that captured path (`crates/c3/src/pack/explain.rs:291`, `crates/c3/src/cli/index.rs:823`) and create a new `.eck/` beside `.c3/`.

`take_over_if_stale` (`crates/c3/src/state_dir.rs:626`) also drops a lock older than 600s while `pid_alive` is still true (`crates/c3/src/state_dir.rs:107`). A `begin_run` stuck in `create_dir_all` (`crates/c3/src/consult/orchestrate/mod.rs:3775`) loses the lock; the new mover can rename, and the first process creates `.eck/` again. Pid reuse with a recorded start time counts as gone (`crates/c3/src/liveness/proc.rs:149`). An empty recorded start time matches any live pid, so that reuse waits out the 10 minutes.

## Q2. Crash points

A kill before `std::fs::rename` (`crates/c3/src/state_dir.rs:735`) leaves leftovers under `.eck/legacy/`; the next `migrate_legacy` renames. A kill after the rename leaves them already moved.

`finish_half_done` (`crates/c3/src/state_dir.rs:930`) runs only when `update_seq` or `telemetry_queue.json` is still at the top (`crates/c3/src/state_dir.rs:73`). An S1 tree whose markers were already moved and whose `anchor` rename failed, or a tree that only had `anchor`, keeps that file at `.c3/anchor`. `read_anchor` (`crates/c3/src/pack/snapshot.rs:657`) treats it as C3's baseline. A linked `lastsnapshot` is noted and does not block the rename (`crates/c3/src/state_dir.rs:896`), so the old report can stay under `lastsnapshot/` and is not retried once the markers are gone. A busy leftover, or a `legacy` that is a link, defers the rename and the next writing command retries; it stops the move only while that obstacle remains.

## Q3. Read-only commands

`c3 pack`, `c3 explain --out`, `c3 index` query/stats, `c3 providers`, `c3 findings`, `c3 consult --status`, `--dry-run`, `c3 work --status`, and `c3 doctor` without `--fix` use `collab_dir` or `read_path` and do not call `migrate_legacy`. `c3 explain` without `--out`, `c3 index` build, `c3 doctor --fix`, finish, init, snapshot, scout, and fetch still move; those are writers. No MCP read path in this diff calls `ensure`.

## Q4. Collab spellings

`sub/../.eck/collab`, `./.eck/collab`, an absolute in-repo path, and a different ASCII case classify as the legacy folder (`crates/c3/src/state_dir.rs:1237`, `crates/c3/src/state_dir.rs:153`).

`repo_relative_normal` returns the lexical path as soon as it lies in the repository (`crates/c3/src/state_dir.rs:1245`), so an in-repo 8.3 name such as `ECK~1/collab` is never canonicalized. A Windows trailing dot or space (`.eck.` or `.eck `) is a different component, and Win32 then creates or opens `.eck`. A first component that is a symlink (`alias/collab` pointing at `.eck`) is not classified; `create_dir_all` follows it. `resolve_collab_root` then canonicalizes (`crates/c3/src/providers.rs:2557`) and follows that link.

## Q5. Live runs and stuck moves

An unlistable directory, an unreadable record, a held `.consult.lock`, and an unreadable start time all fail closed (`crates/c3/src/state_dir.rs:971`, `crates/c3/src/state_dir.rs:1094`, `crates/c3/src/consult/detach.rs:1644`). `begin_run` holds the same lock while the first records are created (`crates/c3/src/state_dir.rs:1196`), so a consultation or work start cannot enter between the check and the rename unless the lock is stolen (Q1).

A directory symlink or junction outside `snapshots`, `lastsnapshot`, `scouts`, `index`, `explains`, and `legacy` makes `walk_runs` report a live run (`crates/c3/src/state_dir.rs:998`) and the move never proceeds. A dead run's ordinary `.consult.lock` is not held, so the move is allowed (`crates/c3/src/state_dir.rs:1173`). The walk is three levels (`crates/c3/src/state_dir.rs:972`); a task at `.eck/a/b/c/<task>` is not inspected. A lock whose owner is gone is removed (`crates/c3/src/state_dir.rs:611`).

## Q6. Links

`link_problem` (`crates/c3/src/state_dir.rs:197`) is enforced by `ensure` and `c3 doctor` only. `c3 consult`, `c3 panel`, and `c3 work` never call it. With `--collab-dir .c3/collab` and `.c3` a symlink, `canonicalize` follows it (`crates/c3/src/providers.rs:2557`) and `create_dir_all` follows it (`crates/c3/src/consult/orchestrate/mod.rs:3775`). `read_path` uses `Path::is_dir` (`crates/c3/src/state_dir.rs:139`), so a symlinked `.eck` is read through. A component swapped for a link between the metadata check and `rename` (`crates/c3/src/state_dir.rs:705`, `crates/c3/src/state_dir.rs:735`) is not caught; on Unix the rename moves the link, so `.c3` becomes that link. A hard link is not `is_link` (`crates/c3/src/setup/repo_models.rs:463`); `write_in` truncates every name. `git_common_dir` uses following `metadata` (`crates/c3/src/state_dir.rs:534`), so a symlinked `.git` directory receives the lock file.

## Q7. Claims

The switch matches the code: with `C3_STATE_MIGRATE=off`, C3 does not rename `.eck/`, creates `.c3/` for its own files, and uses a collab path under `.eck/` as given (README.md:707, `crates/c3/src/state_dir.rs:1383`).

CHANGELOG.md:518 says the lock is taken over only when the owner is gone; the 600s rule also takes it from a live owner. README.md:697 says any leftover `anchor` is repaired; that happens only while a marker file is still at the top. README.md:710 and CHANGELOG.md:527 say every writing command refuses a `.c3` link and that C3 never reads through a link; consult and `read_path` still follow one.

## Q8. Untested

Nothing holds the mover past the lock wait and then checks `c3 explain` or `c3 index` for a second `.eck/`. Nothing points `c3 consult` at a symlinked `.c3`. Nothing is a half-done `.c3/` that contains only `anchor`. Nothing covers a Windows trailing dot, an 8.3 component, or a symlink component. `nested_state_folders_are_kept_out_of_a_diff_patch` covers a committed nested `--diff` exclusion; I did not run it. The check-then-rename swap is untested.

## Requested checks

RC1. In a disposable repo, hold `CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_STATE_MOVE_HOLD` past 10s inside `migrate_legacy` and run `c3 explain` with no `--out`. Workspace-write, about 1 minute. Finding #2: a new `.eck/` appears beside `.c3/` and the explainer file is in the new folder.

RC2. Point `<repo>/.c3` at an outside directory that already has `collab/`, then run `c3 consult --collab-dir .c3/collab` with a fake engine that returns immediately. Workspace-write, about 1 minute. Finding #1: the outside `collab/` gains a task directory and the command does not refuse.

RC3. Put a non-empty `anchor` at the top of `.c3/` and omit `update_seq` and `telemetry_queue.json`, then run `c3 snapshot --delta`. Workspace-write, about 1 minute. Finding #3: the snapshot uses that file as C3's baseline.

findings.claim: A symlinked .c3 or .eck is still followed by consult, panel, and work. link_problem refuses only inside ensure and c3 doctor. resolve_collab_root canonicalizes the collab path, and create_dir_all follows an intermediate symlink, so --collab-dir .c3/collab writes the task directory into the link target. read_path uses Path::is_dir, so read-only commands also read through a symlinked .eck. README.md:710 says C3 never reads or writes through a link and that every writing command refuses a .c3 link.
findings.trigger: The repository's .c3 is a symlink to a directory, and c3 consult, c3 panel, or c3 work is started with --collab-dir .c3/collab. The same follow happens for --collab-dir .eck/collab when .eck itself is a symlink.

evidence.observation: After collab_dir or collab_dir_moving returns, resolve_collab_root_with always std::fs::canonicalize's the path, which follows symlinks, and falls back to the uncanonical path when canonicalize fails.
link_problem is implemented and called from ensure and doctor. A repo-wide search shows no other caller, so consult, panel, and work never refuse a .c3 link.
read_path rejects a .c3 link, then returns .eck when Path::is_dir is true. Path::is_dir follows a symlink, so the returned path is the link and later reads follow it.

findings.verification: RC2: point .c3 at an outside directory and run c3 consult --collab-dir .c3/collab; the outside collab directory receives the task files and the process does not print the link refusal.
findings.remedy: Before any writing command uses a collab path, refuse when .c3 or .eck is a link, using the same link_problem test as ensure. Do that on the path before canonicalize, and make read_path use symlink_metadata for .eck the way it already does for .c3.

findings.claim: A process that loses the move lock, or has the lock taken over while it still lives, can create a second .eck after the winner renames. after_failure adopts .eck whenever .c3 is not there yet. c3 explain (no --out) and c3 index then create_dir_all that path with no later remap. take_over_if_stale removes a lock older than 600 seconds even when the owner is alive, which CHANGELOG.md:518 does not say.
findings.trigger: One process holds the move lock inside migrate_legacy for more than 10 seconds before renaming (a large live-run walk, or a leftover rename that blocks and then succeeds), while c3 explain with no --out or c3 index build is waiting. Separately, a begin_run that still holds the lock after 10 minutes has it removed and the folder renamed underneath its create_dir_all.

evidence.observation: Acquire returns the holder text after lock_wait (default 10s). after_failure sets deferred only when .c3 is absent and .eck exists, so the caller is told to use .eck while the holder has not renamed yet.
explain prepares the legacy explains directory and then create_dir_all's that parent and writes the file. It does not call write_in or moved_with_folder at the write.
A parsed lock is stale when the owner is gone or when file age is greater than LOCK_STALE_SECS (600). The age clause does not require the owner to be dead.

findings.verification: RC1: hold CODEX_CONSULT_TEST_STATE_MOVE_HOLD past 10s and run c3 explain with no --out; after the holder renames, compare the explainer path with .c3/explains and see whether a new .eck/ exists.
findings.remedy: Have explain and index write through write_in or prepare_dir at the write itself, and refuse to create .eck when it is absent. Take a lock over only when the owner is gone, or keep the wait until the holder drops the lock instead of proceeding on the legacy path.

findings.claim: A half-done .c3 that has the old tool's anchor and no longer has update_seq or telemetry_queue.json at its top is never repaired. finish_half_done requires one of those two markers, and read_anchor then uses the leftover anchor as C3's snapshot baseline. README.md:697 says any anchor an earlier build left at the top is put right.
findings.trigger: An S1 move already renamed .eck to .c3, moved update_seq and telemetry_queue.json into legacy/, and failed or was killed before moving anchor. Or the old folder contained only anchor. A later c3 snapshot --delta or c3 finish --snapshot runs.

evidence.observation: HALF_DONE_MARKERS lists only update_seq and telemetry_queue.json. finish_half_done returns immediately when neither name exists at the top, so a lone anchor is left in place. The comment says C3's own anchor must stay, which is why anchor alone is not a marker.

The S1 loop renamed the folder first and then moved leftovers one by one, continuing after a single rename failure. A failed anchor rename after the markers had moved leaves exactly the state finish_half_done now ignores.
read_anchor reads state_dir/anchor and accepts any non-empty trimmed string, with no check that the file lives under legacy/.

findings.verification: RC3: write only anchor at the top of .c3 and run c3 snapshot --delta; the delta base is that file's contents.
findings.remedy: Treat a top-level anchor as half-done when legacy/ already holds the old markers, or when anchor's bytes are not a C3 snapshot id. Keep a C3-written anchor where it is when those signs are absent.

findings.claim: Collab spellings that the file system treats as .eck are not classified, so after the move a writer can create a new .eck. An in-repo 8.3 component is returned before canonicalization. A Windows trailing dot or space is a different component and Win32 maps it back to .eck. A symlink used as the first component is not a state path, and prepare_dir's create_dir_all follows it.
findings.trigger: After .eck has been renamed to .c3, a command is given --collab-dir .eck. or .eck /collab on Windows, or ECK~1/collab where that is the short name of the old folder, or alias/collab where alias is a symlink to .eck.

evidence.observation: repo_relative_normal returns the lexical repo-relative path as soon as repo_relative succeeds. canonical_prefix runs only when the lexical path is outside the repository, so an in-repo short name is never expanded.
names_equal folds ASCII case on Windows and macOS and otherwise compares bytes. .eck. and ECK~1 are not equal to .eck, so split_state_path returns None and resolve_collab returns the path unchanged.
A path that does not classify as .c3 or .eck is created with create_dir_all, which follows intermediate links and, on Windows, the trailing-dot normalization of the API.

findings.verification: On Windows, after a completed move, run a writer with --collab-dir .eck./collab and list the repository root for a new .eck directory.
findings.remedy: Canonicalize with the platform's full-path rules, including trailing dots and short names, before classification, and treat a symlink component that resolves inside .c3 or .eck as that folder.

findings.claim: Two link cases remain around the move. A directory symlink or junction anywhere in the three-level walk, outside the six skipped names, blocks the move for good and every later writing command reports that a run may be live. Between the metadata check and rename, a component swapped for a link is not rechecked; a hard link is not classified as a link, so write_in updates every name that shares the file.
findings.trigger: .eck contains a directory junction that is not snapshots, lastsnapshot, scouts, index, explains, or legacy, and any writing command runs. Or a local writer replaces .eck with a symlink after the locked metadata check and before rename, or hard-links .c3/JOURNAL.md outside the repository before a finish write.

evidence.observation: A link that is not in NOT_RUN_PLACES and whose followed metadata is a directory, or whose metadata cannot be read, returns immediately as a possible live run. Nothing later distinguishes a user junction from a task.
The locked re-check uses symlink_metadata, then relocate_leftovers, then std::fs::rename on the same path. There is no directory handle tying the rename to the directory that was checked.
is_link is symlink on Unix and any reparse point on Windows. A hard link has neither, so the write path does not refuse it.

findings.verification: Put a directory junction under .eck/collab-link and run c3 finish; the command keeps using .eck and the note says a run may be live. Repeat with the junction removed and the move completes.
findings.remedy: Name the blocking link in the deferral and document that removing it unblocks the move. For the rename, open the directory and rename that handle, and refuse a destination whose link count is greater than one when the bytes would change.

Untracked nested .c3/.eck files in a working-tree --diff were not executed; the unit test covers a committed range.
